Class HttpUrlExtractor

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.instrumentation.HttpUrlExtractor
public final class HttpUrlExtractor extends Object
Reflective URL-extraction helpers for intercepted HTTP client calls.

All client types (okhttp3.Call, Apache HttpComponents request classes, Reactor Netty HttpClient) are compileOnly dependencies in the agent. (The JDK HttpClient advice reads HttpRequest.uri() directly and needs no extraction.) They may or may not be on the application classpath at runtime. Accessing them via Method.invoke(Object, Object...) keeps the instrumentation module free of any hard link.

Failures are swallowed and returned as null — the caller treats a null URL as "no URL filter will match" which matches the NamePattern.any() selector default.

  • Method Details

    • okHttpCallFailed

      public static Throwable okHttpCallFailed(Object call, Throwable rejected)
      Ends an OkHttp call the agent rejected the way OkHttp ends a call whose network failed. getResponseWithInterceptorChain throws what noMoreExchanges(e) returns for an IOException its chain threw: that releases the call, exits its timeout (an expired call timeout turns the failure into an InterruptedIOException) and reports EventListener.callFailed. For any other failure its finally calls noMoreExchanges(null), which reports callEnd. The reject is thrown from the advice before that body runs, so the advice runs this same step. Only the lookup is agent-internal; noMoreExchanges itself runs as the application's code, as it does in OkHttp.
      Parameters:
      call - the RealCall
      rejected - what the dispatch threw
      Returns:
      what to throw: noMoreExchanges' answer for an IOException, else rejected; also rejected when the call has no such method (OkHttp 3) or it cannot be made callable, and the listener's own failure when it throws, as OkHttp lets it propagate
